facts.claim: The server is the npm package mcp-sqlite, started with npx -y and the database path as its only argument; npm latest is 1.0.9 (published 2026-04-04).
facts.evidence: README: args ["-y", "mcp-sqlite", "<path-to-your-sqlite-database.db>"], 'Your database path must be provided as an argument.'; registry dist-tags latest 1.0.9.

facts.claim: The package ships a Node.js bin (mcp-sqlite-server.js) and depends on sqlite3 and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.
facts.evidence: bin mcp-sqlite-server -> mcp-sqlite-server.js; engines node >=14; README launches it with npx.

facts.claim: Tools: db_info and list_tables (no input), get_table_schema, read_records (read); create_record, update_records, delete_records (change rows); query (any SQL).
facts.evidence: README sections: Database Information, CRUD Operations, Custom Queries.

facts.claim: query executes an arbitrary SQL statement against the connected database.
facts.evidence: 'Execute a custom SQL query against the connected SQLite database.'

facts.claim: The MCP project's SQLite reference server is archived (servers-archived, 'no longer maintained') and its SQL-injection flaw reported by Trend Micro in June 2025 will not be patched.
facts.evidence: Trend Micro: no patch is planned; GitHub API: modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived archived=true, src/sqlite present; The Register 2025-06-25 reports the same.

facts.claim: Google's MCP Toolbox prebuilt sqlite config reads the database path only from the SQLITE_DATABASE environment variable and offers execute_sql and list_tables.
facts.evidence: 'SQLITE_DATABASE: The path to the SQLite database file'; the prebuilt YAML has database: ${SQLITE_DATABASE} (same repository, so one source).

facts.claim: mcp-sqlite is a community project (jparkerweb, eQuill Labs, MIT), not archived, last pushed 2026-04-05; releases 1.0.8 (2026-03-15) and 1.0.9 (2026-04-04).
facts.evidence: GitHub API archived=false pushed_at 2026-04-05; npm time shows 1.0.8 and 1.0.9 dates.

choices.decision: mcp-sqlite@1.0.9 (stdio-npx) with the file as the {db} parameter
choices.because: The reference server is archived with an unfixed SQL injection; Google's Toolbox is maintained but takes the path only from an environment variable, which a template parameter cannot fill; mcp-sqlite is maintained and takes the path on the command line.

choices.decision: consent on query, update_records, delete_records; explicit read for the four look-only tools
choices.because: query runs any SQL; update and delete change rows irreversibly; the read tools would otherwise be classed as writes by name.
read-only and takes no input per the README

open: mcp-sqlite is a community server, not a vendor's. The skill prefers official sources; there is no maintained official SQLite MCP server that takes a path argument.
Switching to Google's MCP Toolbox needs lotr to substitute template params into connect.env (today apply_params fills connect.command only).
Tool names and their read/write nature come from the README only; not checked against tools/list or the source.
Whether mcp-sqlite builds its own SQL from table and column names safely was not reviewed; the consent list limits what runs without a person.
The npm pin rests on the registry; the README shows the command unpinned.
